images.caption:
49°55'n 6°19'w Known as 49 degrees for short this shop celebrates the fact that the Islands lie south of 50 degrees North in latitude. Set up as an off-shoot of the already successful Foredeck clothes shop it opened some time in the 1990s.  Prior to that the building had housed the St Mary's Bulb Shop.
No Scillonian holiday is complete without checking-out this year's designs and buying a tee-shirt or jumper.

images.filename: Back Lane, Hugh Town, St. Mary's - geograph.org.uk - 924219.jpg
images.caption: Back Lane, Hugh Town, St. Mary's Serving the rear of the properties in both Higher Strand and Church Street. Now limited to pedestrian only access from the eastern end. Newer developments at the rear of the houses (such as "The Aft Cabin" on the right) provide simple, but very comfortable self-catering holiday accommodation in great demand from the tourists. Beats camping when the weather turns bad!

images.filename: Coronation shelter, The Strand , Hugh Town, St. Mary's - geograph.org.uk - 932809.jpg
images.caption: Coronation shelter, The Strand , Hugh Town, St. Mary's A year late in construction, the plaque reads: "This Shelter was erected in 1954 to commemorate the coronation of Her Majesty Queen Elizabeth II by the council of the Isles of Scilly with the assistance of the McDonald Trust".The harbour can be seen on the right. The large grey building high up on the left is the Duchy of Cornwall Offices.
